════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MOTOR CONTRIBUTION TO SHORT CIRCUIT
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Motor: 50 HP Fire pump motor
HP: 50
Type: induction
Motor Bus Voltage: 440V
⚠️  Fault Voltage: 13200V (impedance will be referred)
Efficiency: 90.0%
Power Factor: 0.85

IEEE 141 Classification: induction_medium
X/R Ratio: 4.5
X" (Subtransient Reactance): 17% on motor base
Contribution Factor: 4× FLC (interrupting)

FULL LOAD CURRENT:
FLC = (HP × 746 W/HP) / (√3 × V × η × PF)
FLC = (50 × 746) / (1.7321 × 440 × 0.900 × 0.85)
FLC = 63.98 A

LOCKED ROTOR CURRENT (Approximate):
LRC ≈ 4 × FLC = 4 × 63.98
LRC ≈ 255.91 A

MOTOR IMPEDANCE (at 440V):
Z_motor = V / (√3 × I_LRC)
Z_motor = 440 / (1.7321 × 255.91)
Z_motor = 0.992654 Ω

Component Separation (X/R = 4.5):
X_motor = 0.969016 Ω
R_motor = 0.215337 Ω

⚠️  VOLTAGE LEVEL CORRECTION:
Motor at 440V, Fault at 13200V
Voltage Ratio: 30.0000

Impedance Referred to 13200V:
  R_referred = 0.215337 × 30.0000² = 193.803228 Ω
  X_referred = 0.969016 × 30.0000² = 872.114528 Ω
  Z_referred = 893.388740 Ω

Current Referred to 13200V:
  I_referred = 255.91 / 30.0000 = 8.53 A

MOTOR FAULT CONTRIBUTION (at 13200V):
I_motor = V_fault / (√3 × Z_referred)
I_motor = 13200 / (1.7321 × 893.388740)
I_motor = 8.53 A = 0.009 kA

ASYMMETRICAL CONTRIBUTION:
Multiplier = √(1 + 2e^(-4R/X)) = 1.3499
I_asym = 0.009 × 1.3499
I_asym = 0.012 kA

Per IEEE 141-1993:
  • Motor contribution decays rapidly (typically 3-5 cycles)
  • Primarily affects momentary/instantaneous duty
  • Must be considered for breaker interrupting ratings
  • NEC 430.52 requires motor contribution in fault calculations

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHORT CIRCUIT CALCULATION - PER-UNIT METHOD
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

📋 CALCULATION INFORMATION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Date/Time:           2025-11-11 07:13:26 UTC
Engineer:            B. P. Faraon
Temperature:         75°C
Method:              Per-Unit System
System Frequency:    60 Hz
Breaker Contact:     50.00 ms
Motor Time Point:    3 cycles

📊 PER-UNIT BASE VALUES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Base kVA:            10000 kVA
Base Voltage:        13200 V
Base Impedance:      17.424000 Ω
Base Current:        437.39 A

📖 METHODOLOGY NOTES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Per-unit method automatically handles voltage level changes
• Transformer ratios built into per-unit conversion
• Zero sequence (Z0) tracked for line-to-ground faults
• Component tags shown for full traceability
• From/To bus connections displayed
• All impedances normalized to common 10000 kVA base

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STEP 1: SOURCE BUS IMPEDANCE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

🔌 SOURCE INFORMATION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Bus Tag:             MERALCO-CCP
Bus Name:            MERALCO-CCP
Bus Type:            SOURCE
Voltage Level:       13200 V
Available Fault:     4.37 kA
X/R Ratio:           6

📐 IMPEDANCE CALCULATION (OHMIC)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Formula:             Z_source = V_LL / (√3 × I_sc)

Step-by-Step:
   Z = 13200 / (1.7321 × 4373.865675678983)
   Z = 13200 / 7575.76
   Z = 1.742400 Ω

Component Separation (X/R = 6):
   R = Z / √(1 + (X/R)²) = 0.286449 Ω
   X = R × (X/R) = 1.718693 Ω

Positive Sequence (Z1):
   R1 = 0.286449 Ω
   X1 = 1.718693 Ω

Zero Sequence (Z0 = 1.5× Z1):
   R0 = 0.429673 Ω
   X0 = 2.578039 Ω

📊 CONVERSION TO PER-UNIT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Base Impedance at 13200V:
   Formula:          Z_base = V² / S_base
   Z_base = (13200)² / (10000 × 1000)
   Z_base = 174240000 / 10000000
   Z_base = 17.424000 Ω

Per-Unit Conversion:
   Formula:          Z_pu = Z_ohms / Z_base
   R_pu = 0.286449 / 17.424000 = 0.016440 pu
   X_pu = 1.718693 / 17.424000 = 0.098639 pu
   R0_pu = 0.429673 / 17.424000 = 0.024660 pu
   X0_pu = 2.578039 / 17.424000 = 0.147959 pu

✅ RUNNING TOTALS (Per-Unit)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   Z1: R_pu = 0.016440, X_pu = 0.098639
   Z0: R0_pu = 0.024660, X0_pu = 0.147959

I_motor = 13200 / (1.7321 × 4466.943700)
I_motor = 1.71 A = 0.002 kA

ASYMMETRICAL CONTRIBUTION:
Multiplier = √(1 + 2e^(-4R/X)) = 1.2542
I_asym = 0.002 × 1.2542
I_asym = 0.002 kA

Per IEEE 141-1993:
  • Motor contribution decays rapidly (typically 3-5 cycles)
  • Primarily affects momentary/instantaneous duty
  • Must be considered for breaker interrupting ratings
  • NEC 430.52 requires motor contribution in fault calculations

MOTOR CONTRIBUTION TO SHORT CIRCUIT
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Motor: 50 HP Fire pump motor
HP: 50
Type: induction
Motor Bus Voltage: 440V
⚠️  Fault Voltage: 13200V (impedance will be referred)
Efficiency: 90.0%
Power Factor: 0.85

IEEE 141 Classification: induction_medium
X/R Ratio: 4.5
X" (Subtransient Reactance): 17% on motor base
Contribution Factor: 4× FLC (interrupting)

FULL LOAD CURRENT:
FLC = (HP × 746 W/HP) / (√3 × V × η × PF)
FLC = (50 × 746) / (1.7321 × 440 × 0.900 × 0.85)
FLC = 63.98 A

LOCKED ROTOR CURRENT (Approximate):
LRC ≈ 4 × FLC = 4 × 63.98
LRC ≈ 255.91 A

MOTOR IMPEDANCE (at 440V):
Z_motor = V / (√3 × I_LRC)
Z_motor = 440 / (1.7321 × 255.91)
Z_motor = 0.992654 Ω

Component Separation (X/R = 4.5):
X_motor = 0.969016 Ω
R_motor = 0.215337 Ω

⚠️  VOLTAGE LEVEL CORRECTION:
Motor at 440V, Fault at 13200V
Voltage Ratio: 30.0000

Impedance Referred to 13200V:
  R_referred = 0.215337 × 30.0000² = 193.803228 Ω
  X_referred = 0.969016 × 30.0000² = 872.114528 Ω
  Z_referred = 893.388740 Ω

Current Referred to 13200V:
  I_referred = 255.91 / 30.0000 = 8.53 A

MOTOR FAULT CONTRIBUTION (at 13200V):
I_motor = V_fault / (√3 × Z_referred)
I_motor = 13200 / (1.7321 × 893.388740)
I_motor = 8.53 A = 0.009 kA

ASYMMETRICAL CONTRIBUTION:

📏 STEP 3: ARC FLASH BOUNDARY
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The arc flash boundary is the distance at which the incident energy
equals 1.2 cal/cm² (onset of second-degree burn).

Boundary Calculation:
  Target Energy (Eb):      1.2 cal/cm² (second-degree burn threshold)
  Incident Energy (E):     848.86 cal/cm² at 36"
  Working Distance (Dw):   36 inches

  Formula: Db = Dw × √(E / Eb)
  Db = 36 × √(848.86 / 1.2)
  Db = 36 × 26.5966
  Db = 957.48 inches

📊 IEEE 1584-2018 LOW VOLTAGE METHOD
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Voltage Range: 208V - 600V

Arc Power Calculation:
  log₁₀(Iarc) = log₁₀(22160) = 4.3456
  log₁₀(E) = k + 0.662×log(Iarc) + 0.0966×V + ...
  log₁₀(E) = 3.5818
  Arc Power = 10^3.5818 = 3817.91 W

Incident Energy Formula:
  E = 4.184 × Carc × t × (610²) / (D² × 10000)
  Where:
    Carc = Arc power = 3817.91 W
    t = Exposure time = 0.033 sec
    D = Working distance = 457 mm
    610 = Normalization constant (mm)

  E = 4.184 × 3817.91 × 0.033 × 372100 / (457² × 10000)
  E = 0.09 cal/cm²

📏 STEP 3: ARC FLASH BOUNDARY
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The arc flash boundary is the distance at which the incident energy
equals 1.2 cal/cm² (onset of second-degree burn).

Boundary Calculation:
  Target Energy (Eb):      1.2 cal/cm² (second-degree burn threshold)
  Incident Energy (E):     0.09 cal/cm² at 18"
  Working Distance (Dw):   18 inches

  Formula: Db = Dw × √(E / Eb)
  Db = 18 × √(0.09 / 1.2)
  Db = 18 × 0.2810
  Db = 5.06 inches

  log₁₀(Iarc) = log₁₀(22073) = 4.3439

  Where:
    Carc = Arc power = 3805.74 W
    t = Exposure time = 0.033 sec
    D = Working distance = 457 mm
    610 = Normalization constant (mm)

  E = 4.184 × 3805.74 × 0.033 × 372100 / (457² × 10000)
  E = 0.09 cal/cm²

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

equals 1.2 cal/cm² (onset of second-degree burn).

  Incident Energy (E):     0.09 cal/cm² at 18"
  Working Distance (Dw):   18 inches

  Formula: Db = Dw × √(E / Eb)

📊 IEEE 1584-2018 LOW VOLTAGE METHOD
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Voltage Range: 208V - 600V

Arc Power Calculation:
  log₁₀(Iarc) = log₁₀(8570) = 3.9330
  log₁₀(E) = k + 0.662×log(Iarc) + 0.0966×V + ...
  log₁₀(E) = 3.2474
  Arc Power = 10^3.2474 = 1767.63 W

Incident Energy Formula:
  E = 4.184 × Carc × t × (610²) / (D² × 10000)
  Where:
    Carc = Arc power = 1767.63 W
    t = Exposure time = 0.033 sec
    D = Working distance = 457 mm
    610 = Normalization constant (mm)

  E = 4.184 × 1767.63 × 0.033 × 372100 / (457² × 10000)
  E = 0.04 cal/cm²

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

equals 1.2 cal/cm² (onset of second-degree burn).

Boundary Calculation:
  Target Energy (Eb):      1.2 cal/cm² (second-degree burn threshold)
  Incident Energy (E):     0.04 cal/cm² at 18"
  Working Distance (Dw):   18 inches

  Formula: Db = Dw × √(E / Eb)

📊 IEEE 1584-2018 LOW VOLTAGE METHOD
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Voltage Range: 208V - 600V

Arc Power Calculation:
  log₁₀(Iarc) = log₁₀(9094) = 3.9587
  log₁₀(E) = k + 0.662×log(Iarc) + 0.0966×V + ...
  log₁₀(E) = 3.2683
  Arc Power = 10^3.2683 = 1854.63 W

Incident Energy Formula:
  E = 4.184 × Carc × t × (610²) / (D² × 10000)
  Where:
    Carc = Arc power = 1854.63 W
    t = Exposure time = 0.033 sec
    D = Working distance = 457 mm
    610 = Normalization constant (mm)

  E = 4.184 × 1854.63 × 0.033 × 372100 / (457² × 10000)
  E = 0.05 cal/cm²

📏 STEP 3: ARC FLASH BOUNDARY
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The arc flash boundary is the distance at which the incident energy
equals 1.2 cal/cm² (onset of second-degree burn).

Boundary Calculation:
  Target Energy (Eb):      1.2 cal/cm² (second-degree burn threshold)
  Incident Energy (E):     0.05 cal/cm² at 18"
  Working Distance (Dw):   18 inches

  Formula: Db = Dw × √(E / Eb)
  Db = 18 × √(0.05 / 1.2)
  Db = 18 × 0.1959
  Db = 3.53 inches

📊 IEEE 1584-2018 LOW VOLTAGE METHOD
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Voltage Range: 208V - 600V

Arc Power Calculation:
  log₁₀(Iarc) = log₁₀(10214) = 4.0092
  log₁₀(E) = k + 0.662×log(Iarc) + 0.0966×V + ...
  log₁₀(E) = 3.3091
  Arc Power = 10^3.3091 = 2037.71 W

Incident Energy Formula:
  E = 4.184 × Carc × t × (610²) / (D² × 10000)
  Where:
    Carc = Arc power = 2037.71 W
    t = Exposure time = 0.033 sec
    D = Working distance = 457 mm
    610 = Normalization constant (mm)

  E = 4.184 × 2037.71 × 0.033 × 372100 / (457² × 10000)
  E = 0.05 cal/cm²

🔥 INCIDENT ENERGY RESULT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Hazard Level:                ✅ LIMITED (< 1.2 cal/cm²)

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
📏 STEP 3: ARC FLASH BOUNDARY
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The arc flash boundary is the distance at which the incident energy
equals 1.2 cal/cm² (onset of second-degree burn).

Boundary Calculation:
  Target Energy (Eb):      1.2 cal/cm² (second-degree burn threshold)
  Incident Energy (E):     0.05 cal/cm² at 18"
  Working Distance (Dw):   18 inches

  Formula: Db = Dw × √(E / Eb)
  Db = 18 × √(0.05 / 1.2)
  Db = 18 × 0.2053
  Db = 3.70 inches

📐 IMPEDANCE CALCULATION (OHMIC)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Formula:             Z_source = V_LL / (√3 × I_sc)

Step-by-Step:
   Z = 13200 / (1.7321 × 4373.865675678983)
   Z = 13200 / 7575.76
   Z = 1.742400 Ω

Component Separation (X/R = 6):
   R = Z / √(1 + (X/R)²) = 0.286449 Ω
   X = R × (X/R) = 1.718693 Ω

Positive Sequence (Z1):
   R1 = 0.286449 Ω
   X1 = 1.718693 Ω

Zero Sequence (Z0 = 1.5× Z1):
   R0 = 0.429673 Ω
   X0 = 2.578039 Ω

📊 CONVERSION TO PER-UNIT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Base Impedance at 13200V:
   Formula:          Z_base = V² / S_base

📊 IEEE 1584-2018 LOW VOLTAGE METHOD
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Voltage Range: 208V - 600V

Arc Power Calculation:
  log₁₀(Iarc) = log₁₀(10751) = 4.0315
  log₁₀(E) = k + 0.662×log(Iarc) + 0.0966×V + ...
  log₁₀(E) = 3.3272
  Arc Power = 10^3.3272 = 2124.27 W

Incident Energy Formula:
  E = 4.184 × Carc × t × (610²) / (D² × 10000)
  Where:
    Carc = Arc power = 2124.27 W
    t = Exposure time = 0.033 sec
    D = Working distance = 457 mm
    610 = Normalization constant (mm)

  E = 4.184 × 2124.27 × 0.033 × 372100 / (457² × 10000)
  E = 0.05 cal/cm²

Hazard Level:                ✅ LIMITED (< 1.2 cal/cm²)

📏 STEP 3: ARC FLASH BOUNDARY
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The arc flash boundary is the distance at which the incident energy
equals 1.2 cal/cm² (onset of second-degree burn).

Boundary Calculation:
  Target Energy (Eb):      1.2 cal/cm² (second-degree burn threshold)
  Incident Energy (E):     0.05 cal/cm² at 18"
  Working Distance (Dw):   18 inches

  Formula: Db = Dw × √(E / Eb)
  Db = 18 × √(0.05 / 1.2)
  Db = 18 × 0.2096
  Db = 3.77 inches
